title: Zooplankton reliance on autochthonous and allochthonous resources across mountain lakes revealed through essential amino acid δ13C analysis
content:
Abstract

Terrestrial subsidies shape aquatic ecosystem structure and function, serving as important energy channels for consumers when phytoplankton and other autochthonous resources are limited. Despite this, quantifying the assimilation of allochthonous nutrients by aquatic consumers can be challenging. Here, we show terrestrial plants, benthic algae, and particulate organic matter have distinct essential amino acid (AAESS) carbon isotope (δ13C) fingerprints across eight freshwater habitats in California's eastern Sierra Nevada Mountains, which enabled us to quantify the relative contributions of autochthonous and allochthonous resources to zooplankton. We found in-water production accounted for the majority (70–98%) of AAESS assimilated by zooplankton, with low but variable zooplankton allochthony (2–30%) across zooplankton taxa and habitats. Assimilation of terrestrial plant-derived AAESS differed among zooplankton groups, with the lowest assimilation in Calanoida (7%), intermediate assimilation in a pooled > 350 μm zooplankton fraction (10%) and Cladocera (17%), and highest in Neocopepoda (calanoids and cyclopoids; 24%). Zooplankton allochthony also positively correlated with elevation and negatively correlated with chlorophyll a concentrations, indicating geographic factors and primary production are strong predictors of terrestrial plant-derived AAESS use by lacustrine zooplankton in mountain lakes. These findings suggest there is interspecific variation in the mechanisms employed by zooplankton to access terrestrial carbon pools and illustrate an inverse relationship between primary production and allochthonous support of zooplankton. Our work exemplifies the power of AAESS δ13C fingerprinting in quantifying energy channel utilization in freshwater ecosystems and emphasizes the predominance of autochthonous nutrition to zooplankton in alpine and montane lakes.
